---
title: "Research"
---

I'm interested in how people move between education and work, and in what
policy can actually do about it.

## Current questions

**How do students choose fields of study, and how wrong are they about the
returns?** Field choice is one of the highest-stakes decisions a young person
makes, usually with poor information about what different paths pay and how
that changes over a career.

**What happens when a new institution enters a labor market with no
reputation?** I spent three years on the operating side of this problem at
Plaksha — persuading firms to hire from a university with no placement history.
The question of how employer beliefs about unfamiliar institutions form, and
what shifts them, is one I'd like to study properly rather than only
improvise against.

**Which interventions in the school-to-work transition survive contact with
evidence?** Careers services, internships, employer partnerships and signalling
mechanisms are widely funded and unevenly evaluated.

## Approach

I'm building toward research that takes identification seriously — natural
experiments, administrative data, and causal inference rather than descriptive
correlation. This year that means econometrics coursework and getting fluent
in R and Python. I'll post work here as it develops.
